characters.name: Jane Eyre
characters.description: Narrator and protagonist; orphan raised at Gateshead, pupil and teacher at Lowood, later governess at Thornfield Hall who becomes Rochester’s wife and inherits a fortune.

characters.name: Mrs. Reed
characters.description: Jane’s aunt and guardian at Gateshead Hall; harsh and unsympathetic, later ill and dies.

characters.name: Eliza Reed
characters.description: Eldest daughter of Mrs. Reed; proud, saving, and often unkind to Jane.

characters.name: John Reed
characters.description: Son of Mrs. Reed; a bullying, cruel youth who torments Jane; later dies.

characters.name: Georgiana Reed
characters.description: Younger daughter of Mrs. Reed; beautiful, self-indulgent, and somewhat vain.

characters.name: Bessie (Mrs. Leaven)
characters.description: Nursery maid at Gateshead who cares for Jane at times; later marries Robert Leaven and visits Gateshead.

characters.name: Abbot (Miss Abbot)
characters.description: A housemaid at Gateshead who often echoes Mrs. Reed’s criticisms of Jane.

characters.name: Mr. Reed (Jane’s uncle)
characters.description: Jane’s deceased uncle (Mrs. Reed’s husband) who originally took Jane in.

characters.name: Mr. Lloyd
characters.description: An apothecary called in to attend at Gateshead; advises sending Jane to school.

characters.name: Mr. Brocklehurst (Rev. Robert Brocklehurst)
characters.description: Religious inspector/manager associated with Lowood School; severe and hypocritical; named treasurer of Lowood in background.

characters.name: Naomi Brocklehurst
characters.description: Benefactor named on the Lowood building tablet (donor mentioned in narrative).

characters.name: Miss Temple (Maria Temple)
characters.description: Superintendent of Lowood; kindly, educated, and a moral guide and friend to Jane.

characters.name: Miss Miller
characters.description: Under-teacher at Lowood who oversees classes and duties.

characters.name: Miss Smith
characters.description: Teacher at Lowood responsible for work and domestic training.

characters.name: Miss Scatcherd
characters.description: A harsh teacher at Lowood who punishes and criticises pupils (notably Helen Burns).

characters.name: Madame Pierrot
characters.description: French teacher at Lowood (from Lille), teaches French to pupils including Jane.

characters.name: Helen Burns
characters.description: Pupil at Lowood; devout, patient, and a close friend of Jane who dies of consumption.

characters.name: Rev. Mr. Nasmyth
characters.description: Clergyman who marries Miss Temple and leads her to leave Lowood (mentioned in narrative).

characters.name: Richard Mason (Mr. Mason)
characters.description: Traveller from the West Indies who is found wounded at Thornfield and is Bertha Mason’s brother, providing evidence of her existence and marriage to Rochester.

characters.name: Edward Rochester
characters.description: Owner/master of Thornfield Hall; brooding, charismatic, employer and later suitor and husband of Jane; conceals a prior marriage and is injured and temporarily blind after Thornfield’s fire.

characters.name: Grace Poole
characters.description: A Thornfield servant of mysterious habits; employed to attend the madwoman and associated with odd laughter and incidents of fire.

characters.name: Mrs. Fairfax
characters.description: Housekeeper/manager at Thornfield Hall; practical, kind, and Jane’s immediate superior there.

characters.name: Adèle Varens
characters.description: French pupil at Thornfield; ward of Mr. Rochester, lively and often addressed in French; Jane’s charge.

characters.name: Sophie
characters.description: Adèle’s French nurse (bonne) and servant at Thornfield who dresses Jane and attends the nursery.

characters.name: Leah
characters.description: Housemaid at Thornfield who performs household duties and interacts with other servants; recounts observations about the household.

characters.name: Robert Leaven
characters.description: Coachman who later marries Bessie and returns as a visitor to Gateshead.

characters.name: Mr. Bates
characters.description: Local man (surgeon/attendant) mentioned as being fetched or seen in connection with Mrs. Reed and other events.

characters.name: Mr. Carter (surgeon)
characters.description: Surgeon called to attend Mr. Mason after his injury at Thornfield and who treats related injuries.

characters.name: Pilot (dog)
characters.description: Mr. Rochester’s large dog, companion at Thornfield and affectionate toward Jane and Rochester at Ferndean.

characters.name: Mesrour
characters.description: The name of Mr. Rochester’s black horse mentioned in the narrative.

characters.name: Mrs. Eshton
characters.description: Resident at the Leas; hostess whose daughters visit Thornfield.

characters.name: Amy Eshton
characters.description: One of Mrs. Eshton’s daughters; lively and youthful.

characters.name: Louisa Eshton
characters.description: Another of Mrs. Eshton’s daughters; elegant and pretty.

characters.name: Mr. Eshton
characters.description: Gentleman of the neighbourhood (at the Leas), involved in local visits with Mr. Rochester.

characters.name: Colonel Dent
characters.description: A military gentleman and visitor at Thornfield; organises charades.

characters.name: Mrs. Dent
characters.description: Wife of Colonel Dent, mild and polite.

characters.name: Sir George Lynn
characters.description: Local gentleman, visitor at Thornfield.

characters.name: Henry Lynn
characters.description: Younger Mr. Lynn (frequently called Henry), a lively young man visiting Thornfield.

characters.name: Frederick Lynn
characters.description: Young Mr. Lynn (Frederick), another visitor and part of local set.

characters.name: Lord Ingram
characters.description: A gentleman (peer) visiting Thornfield; brother to Blanche and Mary Ingram.

characters.name: Dowager Lady Ingram
characters.description: Elder matriarch of the Ingram family; proud and imperious.

characters.name: Blanche Ingram
characters.description: Tall, accomplished, and beautiful lady; presented as Mr. Rochester’s anticipated bride.

characters.name: Mary Ingram
characters.description: Blanche’s sister; tall but more passive and languid in expression.

characters.name: Miss Wilson
characters.description: Referenced former governess (mentioned in anecdote).

characters.name: Mrs. Grey
characters.description: Referenced former governess (mentioned in anecdote).

characters.name: Madame Joubert
characters.description: Referenced former governess (mentioned in anecdote).

characters.name: Mr. Vining
characters.description: Referenced tutor (mentioned in anecdote).

characters.name: Mr. Rowland Rochester
characters.description: Mr. Rochester’s elder brother referenced in family background.

characters.name: Bertha Mason
characters.description: Rochester’s first wife, a Creole woman who is mad and confined at Thornfield; responsible for violent outbreaks including setting fires; dies in the blaze that destroys Thornfield.

characters.name: Mr. Briggs
characters.description: Solicitor who produces the marriage record proving Rochester’s prior marriage and communicates legal particulars to interested parties.

characters.name: John Green
characters.description: Clerk present at the church ceremony; named as 'John Green' when the wedding is interrupted.

characters.name: John (Thornfield servant)
characters.description: Servant/coachman/footman at Thornfield mentioned in connection with preparing the carriage and luggage.

characters.name: John (Ferndean servant)
characters.description: Servant at Ferndean Manor who assists Mr. Rochester; appears with his wife Mary in the Ferndean household.

characters.name: Mary (John's wife)
characters.description: Wife of John at Ferndean; assists with domestic tasks and attends Mr. Rochester.

characters.name: Mr. Wood
characters.description: Local clergyman (the officiating minister at the attempted wedding); referred to as 'Mr. Wood' and 'the clergyman'.

characters.name: Hannah (Moor House housekeeper)
characters.description: Long-serving housekeeper/old servant at Moor House who nursed the Rivers siblings and assists Jane and the household.

characters.name: Diana Rivers
characters.description: One of the Rivers sisters; cultivated, studious, and hospitable; she and Mary shelter and nurse Jane at Moor House.

characters.name: Mary Rivers
characters.description: One of the Rivers sisters; gentle and intelligent; shares Moor House with Diana and assists Jane.

characters.name: St. John Rivers
characters.description: Clergyman cousin of Jane (also christened St. John Eyre Rivers); austere, zealous, and missionary-minded; urges Jane to marry him and go to India as a missionary’s wife.

characters.name: Mr. Eyre (of Madeira)
characters.description: Jane’s uncle of Madeira whose death and will make Jane an heiress; referenced as 'Mr. Eyre of Madeira'.

characters.name: Jonas Mason (Mr. Mason Sr.)
characters.description: Father of Bertha Mason cited in the marriage record; appears as part of documentary background.

characters.name: Antoinetta (Mrs. Mason)
characters.description: Mother of Bertha mentioned in the marriage record as a Creole named Antoinetta.

characters.name: Mrs. Poole’s son (keeper at Grimsby Retreat)
characters.description: Referenced attendant related to Grace Poole: Mrs. Poole’s son, keeper at Grimsby Retreat, mentioned as available to assist in paroxysms; unnamed in text.

characters.name: Alice Wood
characters.description: A local woman noted as a helpful, teachable attendant who serves Jane in the schoolhouse context.

characters.name: Mr. Oliver
characters.description: Wealthy proprietor of Vale Hall who funds local projects and supports the Rivers family; father of Rosamond Oliver.

characters.name: Rosamond Oliver
characters.description: Daughter of Mr. Oliver; beautiful, flirtatious heiress who befriends Jane and later becomes engaged and married to Mr. Granby.

characters.name: Mr. Granby
characters.description: Man who ultimately marries Rosamond Oliver; referred to as 'Mr. Granby'.

characters.name: Sir Frederic Granby
characters.description: Elder relation of Mr. Granby (Sir Frederic), referenced as Rosamond’s future family connection.

characters.name: Captain Fitzjames
characters.description: Naval officer mentioned later in the narrative as Diana’s husband; a gallant and good man.

characters.name: Mr. Wharton
characters.description: Clergyman mentioned later as Mary Rivers’s husband.

characters.name: Damer de Rochester
characters.description: An ancestor of the Rochester family whose tomb and kneeling angel monument are described in the church setting (referenced in the narrative).
